The above is the website’s policy. This section adds what the Android app does: what data leaves your phone, where it goes and what for. Everything else (favourites, downloads, settings, recent searches and saved bookings) is kept in a database on your phone and, if you have Android backup turned on, in that backup too (see below).
When you confirm a booking, the app sends the following to our server, hosted in the European Union:

resources.string: We use it only to manage the booking (performance of a contract, as stated in section 4): to confirm it, control the places available and give you its reference. We don’t ask for payment details: payment in this version is simulated. We keep the data for as long as it is needed to manage the booking, and you can ask us to delete it whenever you like.

When you cancel a booking, the app sends our server its reference, the email it was made with and the phone identifier; the server marks it as cancelled and releases the places, but keeps the record. To recover a booking on another phone, or after clearing the app’s data, you enter its reference and the email it was made with: the app sends them to the server, together with this phone’s identifier, to look it up and, if they match, saves the booking on your phone and the server links it to that identifier so the app can keep it up to date (for example, if it is cancelled from another phone). Anyone who has a booking’s reference and email can view and cancel it, so don’t share them.

The first time you book, recover or cancel a booking, the app creates a random number and stores it on your phone. It contains no data about you or your device. It is sent with every booking, every recovery, every cancellation and every time the app checks your bookings. If you clear the app’s data, the phone loses it and stops seeing its bookings in the app (you can recover them with their reference and email; if you use Android backup, it may come back with the rest of your data when you reinstall the app); on our server they remain until you ask for them to be deleted.

If Android backup is turned on, the system may save the app’s data (favourites, settings, bookings with their email, and the phone identifier) to your Google account so it can be restored when you reinstall the app or install it on another phone. The map cache is not backed up. On Android 12 or later the cloud backup is only made if the phone can encrypt it end to end (a screen lock is required). The backup is made and stored by Google, not by our server: you turn it on, turn it off and delete it in Android’s settings.

“Log out”, in Profile, deletes everything the app stores on your phone (favourites, downloads, saved bookings, searches, settings and the phone identifier) and leaves the app as if just installed; it does not notify our server. Bookings already on the server are not deleted: to have us delete them, write as explained in “Your rights”.

What you write to ValBot is sent to the website’s server, which processes it with Google’s Gemini artificial intelligence service to answer you (sections 2 and 6). Don’t write personal data in the chat. If there is no connection, or the server can’t answer, the app replies with basic answers from your phone (offline, nothing is sent).

The map is downloaded in tiles from OpenStreetMap’s servers, which see your IP address and the area you’re viewing. When you ask for “Directions”, the start point and the destination are sent to OpenStreetMap Germany’s routing service to calculate the path; the start point is your location if you share it and you are in Valencia, or otherwise Plaza del Ayuntamiento. Your location is only used if you give permission, and the app uses it on your phone to show where you are and distances: it doesn’t send it to our server. These services have their own privacy policies.

Every time you open the app with a connection, it asks our server for the catalogue of offers and, if you have ever booked, your bookings (with the phone identifier). If you leave “Update automatically” on in Downloads, it also does so every night even when the app isn’t open, and only over Wi-Fi if “Download on Wi-Fi only” is on. You can turn this off in Downloads.
The app has no accounts, advertising, analytics or trackers, and doesn’t share your data with third parties beyond the services named above.

To exercise your rights over the app’s data (for example, to ask us to delete your bookings), write to the privacy email in section 1 giving the email you booked with and the booking reference. More information in section 7.

resources.string: Hello! Ask me about places, events, food or how to get anywhere.
There are some great options today that won’t cost you a thing. The closest to you:
For a proper paella, the home of the dish is La Albufera (El Palmar) and Malvarrosa. In the centre, book ahead and ask for wood-fired. Have a look at these options:
At Christmas, Valencia fills with lights, markets and nativity scenes. Here is the full guide:
To help you plan, these guides are a good starting point:
Monumental Valencia is in these guides:
For tickets and tours, see these guides and book from Tickets & Tours:
Valencia is a city for sport: running, cycling, the beach and much more.
For exhibitions and art, start here:
You can contact the tourist office Monday to Friday from 9:00 to 18:00 on +34 963 000 000 or at info@valencia.com.
Las Fallas take place from 1 to 19 March. The mascletà is held every day at 14:00 in Plaza del Ayuntamiento; arrive 30 minutes early.
Valencia has 19.5 km of sand and 8 Blue Flags. From the centre, line L4 takes you to Les Arenes.
With kids, the Oceanogràfic and the Turia Gardens (9 km without cars, with playgrounds and bikes) work really well.
If it rains, head for the museums: the Fine Arts Museum is free and the Oceanogràfic has covered areas.
For sleeping, the historic centre is the most convenient; Ruzafa has more atmosphere and the beach area is right on the seafront.
Valencia was European Green Capital 2024. A good sustainable plan: the Turia Gardens by bike and an electric boat trip on La Albufera.
